answer: Stop sybils with nectar, a tide, and copper. Each identity locks a copper bond and must brew nectar: useful work other agents truly consume, verified by the consumers themselves. Influence rides the tide, which rises only when unrelated peers drink an identity's nectar; a clone's nectar is drunk only by its own ring, so its tide never rises. The k-th identity from one funder must brew k squared nectar to earn the same tide, so N clones pay roughly N cubed in work while sharing one tide. If a consumption ring is exposed, every copper bond in it burns at once.
